task: Repair the existing Reference Sync so a Git-detected file rename preserves unchanged export identity at the destination while genuinely removed exports and stale old-path consumers remain blocking.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: Reference Sync is a blocking development authority. This defect is a false-positive on safe code movement rather than a missing safety check, but weakening it broadly could create false negatives. The highest proportionate level is a narrow rename-aware identity fix with adversarial tests proving unchanged moved exports are accepted while deleted exports, stale old paths and renamed symbols still block.

acceptanceCriteria: A Git R-status file move with an unchanged export does not create an export-symbol stale-consumer finding merely because the origin path no longer exists.
Consumers that still reference the old file path remain blocking after a rename.
An export genuinely removed during a rename remains an export-symbol candidate and stale consumers remain blocking.
The previously proven export-rename detection for symbol identity changes remains blocking.
invariants: Rename awareness may transfer export identity only from the exact Git old-path to new-path pair reported by name-status.
A same-name export elsewhere in the repository cannot satisfy a moved export unless it is the Git rename destination.
File-path closure and export-symbol closure remain separate checks.
No exception or severity downgrade is introduced.

failureModes: The rename map is ignored when comparing exports, preserving the current false positive.
Any same-name export in a different file is incorrectly accepted as relocation proof.
A real symbol deletion is hidden because the destination file exists.
File-path consumers are mistakenly treated as updated merely because export identity moved.
edgeCases: 100 percent similarity rename with unchanged export.
Rename where a stale old import path remains.
Non-rename edit of the same file.

alternatives.summary: Add exceptions for the pilot acceptance refactor consumers.
alternatives.reason: It would hide a known Reference Sync capability defect and create unsafe precedent for broad exceptions.

alternatives.summary: Make export comparison explicitly follow the exact Git rename destination while leaving old-path closure untouched.
alternatives.reason: It repairs the existing capability at the correct abstraction with minimal behavioral surface and no severity weakening.

alternatives.summary: Disable export-symbol Reference Sync for file moves.
alternatives.reason: That would create a material false-negative class for exports removed or renamed during a move.

specialistReviews.finding: File identity and symbol identity must survive a path move without conflating path closure with export closure.
specialistReviews.resolution: Use the Git rename pair only for export comparison; continue checking old path references independently.

specialistReviews.finding: Relaxing moved-export checks could regress the already proven export-rename blocker.
specialistReviews.resolution: Add negative adversarial cases for rename plus symbol deletion/rename and require stale consumers to remain blocking.

specialistReviews.finding: This is quality-infrastructure-only behavior and should not be bundled into the runtime authority repair.
specialistReviews.resolution: Land it as its own bounded Control Plane transaction before replaying the runtime PR.

challenge.scenario: actions.ts is renamed with 100 percent identical content.
challenge.finding: Current logic compares old path to a now-missing file and falsely marks every export removed.
challenge.resolution: Compare old-path exports to the exact rename destination content.

challenge.scenario: The destination preserves the export but callers still import the old path.
challenge.finding: Export continuity does not prove path continuity.
challenge.resolution: Keep the file-path candidate and stale old-path consumer check unchanged.

challenge.scenario: The file is renamed and the export is deleted.
challenge.finding: A naive rename exemption would create a false negative.
challenge.resolution: Only suppress export candidate when destination exports the same symbol.

challenge.scenario: The file is renamed and the export itself is renamed.
challenge.finding: Old symbol consumers must still block.
challenge.resolution: Old symbol remains a candidate because it is absent from destination exports.

challenge.scenario: Another unrelated file exports the same name.
challenge.finding: Repository-wide name search could falsely satisfy identity.
challenge.resolution: Only the exact Git rename destination is eligible for moved-export continuity.

challenge.scenario: A normal non-rename edit removes an export.
challenge.finding: Rename logic must not alter ordinary removal detection.
challenge.resolution: Use current-file comparison when no rename mapping exists.

proofPlan: Extend the existing Reference Sync self-test with unchanged rename, removed export and stale old-path cases.
Keep the current implementation-expression and asset stale-consumer self-tests green.
Run Plan Before Code, Edit-Time Guard and Incremental Replay on the exact branch head.
Run full Quality tests and exact-head typecheck/build because quality infrastructure changes force full replay.
Replay the pilot acceptance clean rename after this fix without Reference Sync exceptions.

requirements.requirement: Reference Sync must preserve unchanged export identity across the exact Git rename destination.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: An unchanged moved export may not be reported as removed solely because the origin path no longer exists.

requirements.requirement: Old path references and exports removed or renamed during a file move must remain blocking.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Rename awareness may not suppress stale old-path or removed-symbol consumers.

notes: Narrow precursor fix inside the existing Reference Sync authority. No new gate, no exception, no runtime behavior change. The canonical development-guard policy is included as read-only projected authority because the legacy Plan Before Code domain projector intentionally excludes scripts/lib/shoperation-* knowledge infrastructure from direct domain ownership.
